- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–7 days.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.3) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to capture mean reversion.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 2–5 day decay filter to smooth out overreaction.  
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3 days, model often fails to adjust; force a 1–2 day lag correction to align with sentiment reversal.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overpredicts in early days (1–7) when sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish; apply a 0.5–1.5% downward bias to first 7 days.  
- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over 5+ days, model underestimates; apply a 1–2% upward bias to capture potential rebound.  
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, check sentiment for confirmation; if sentiment is weak, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overconfidence.
